result.summary: This PR parallelizes the block-filter-matching step of wallet fast-rescan so that rescanblockchain and wallet loading rescans run up to ~6-8x faster on multi-core machines with a synced block filter index. It introduces a ChainScanner abstraction, a scan-local thread pool, and logic to keep filter verdicts valid as the wallet's script filter set grows during the scan (keypool top-ups). It is split from a larger refactor (#34681) that has since merged, and the PR needs rebasing onto it.
result.problem: Fast rescan is single-threaded today, so users with large wallets or long scan ranges wait a long time (hundreds of seconds in benchmarks) for rescanblockchain or a wallet load that needs to catch up to the tip. This is a common, felt pain point for wallet users and integrators, especially descriptor wallets with block filter indexes.

open_concerns: Design concern from bvbfan/rkrux about using the shared thread pool and having the main thread process tasks (ProcessTask) causing contention with other RPCs — addressed by moving to a scan-local thread pool per author's April update
furszy's suggestion to land the refactor as separate building-block PRs first, which the author did (#34667, #34681)
resolved_concerns: Concerns about shared-threadpool contention resolved by architectural change to a dedicated per-scan thread pool

categories.name: wallet
categories.evidence: PR is labeled Wallet and its entire change is within src/wallet/scan.cpp and related wallet scanning code, directly affecting rescan behavior and correctness.
categories.rationale: P2 because slow rescans are an explicitly named wallet pain point ('user-visible reliability: hangs, slow rescans') and this PR delivers a substantial, independently reproduced speedup (ismaelsadeeq measured 4.5-6.5x, l0rinc and the author measured up to 8x). It is not P1 because it is a performance improvement rather than a fund-safety or consensus fix, though correctness of filter-matching under concurrent top-ups (discussed at length in review, e.g. worst-case scenario analysis) carries some risk if implemented incorrectly, which keeps review attention warranted.

result.card: This PR parallelizes wallet fast-rescan's block-filter checking, giving a well-corroborated 6-8x speedup on multi-core hardware for rescanblockchain and wallet-load catch-up scans, a pain point users of large or old wallets feel directly. Concept support is strong: w0xlt, ismaelsadeeq (who independently reproduced ~4.5-6.5x speedups), and rkrux (Strong Concept ACK) all back the direction, and the main architectural objection about thread-pool contention was resolved when the author switched to a scan-local thread pool. It depends on the now-merged refactor PR #34681 and currently needs a rebase, is marked Needs rebase, and is still in draft with the author silent for roughly two months as of the latest review activity. Priority is P2 in wallet: a real, measured performance win for a named pain point, tempered by it being a performance rather than fund-safety change and by some residual correctness risk in the parallel filter-verdict logic that reviewers have been probing.
